#3762. GTA 6 just got a patch that fixed a progression bug on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S

Rockstar just issued a new patch for GTA 6 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S, targeting a few issues players have been reporting since the game launched last Thursday (19th November).

The 23rd November patch for the game deploys seven major fixes for the game, including a pretty significant bug that prevented phone calls not triggering at certain points, resulting in a scenario where you could be locked out of progressing the game. The official update is titled 'version 01.002.002', and its weighs in at different sizes on different consoles: it's 603.8 MB on PS5, and 1.6 GB on Xbox Series X/S.

Thanks to an update on the Rockstar website, you can read all of the updates that arrive with the latest pathc below.

There have been a few fairly high-profile cases of the autosave not working as the developer intended, leading to a few cases of streamers losing plenty of real-world time thanks to unpredictable auto-save behaviour. JasonTheWeen lost 12 hours of progress on the PS5, for example.

But there's one issue here the developer hasn't addressed: vignetting. Plenty of players have taken to online communities to complain about the vignette effect that pops into the game - theoretically to help with motion smoothing and various grapihcal elements as the game runs in 30FPS. THe effect is worsened when you're fatigued, hungry, or have some other status effect, but it is present quite a lot of the time, too. Most of the responses to a tweet about the patch posted by the Rockstar Support account reference the vignetting in GTA 6, and the developer has issued no response at the time of writing.

If you've played over a hundred hours of Vampire Survivors you've probably forgotten how slow its early progression feels. It certainly seemed that way based on the reaction to Warhammer Survivors from Vampire Survivors veterans, who complained about its grindiness compared to their beloved bullet heaven originator, despite the arc of both games being quite similar. Developers Auroch Digital made Warhammer Survivors in partnership with Vampire Survivors creator Poncle, so of course the two games have a lot in common.

Other complaints were more valid. The Beasts of Nurgle did have too many hit points, and their ability to regenerate only exacerbated that. The treasure chest-opening animation did take a bit too long. And some of the weapons were undertuned. Fortunately, those issues and more have been addressed in hotfix v2.18. Here are the highlights:

The change to XP is an interesting one. It's a standard part of the genre's formula to have random XP drops—killing some enemies gives you nothing, while others drop XP gems and tempt you to rush into a mob to grab them. Making every enemy drop at least a low-value XP gem will speed up leveling a bit, but hopefully when you see green or red gems you'll still want to risk a mob of orks to yoink.

Auroch Digital recently revealed a roadmap of upcoming additions to Warhammer Survivors, with the first big update in December promising more characters, weapons, and weapon evolutions. January's updates will add more quality-of-life and balance improvements, as well as cross-save, with another update in the first quarter of 2027 bringing another round of characters, weapons, and weapon evolutions.

The final item on the roadmap is a tease that simply says, "ERROR… Details classified." It's probably not the addition of a whole extra universe to its current Warhammer 40,000 and Age of Sigmar settings, but I'd be stoked to see them add the other popular world of Warhammer. By which I mean Blood Bowl, of course.

#3759. Dawn of War 4's newest trailer teases the appearance of a fan-favourite character in the game's post-launch DLC

As Dawn of War 4's December release date inches ever closer, a new trailer appears to have teased a fan-favourite character's inclusion in the RTS's first post-launch DLC.

The trailer, which covers the Commander Edition of Dawn of War 4, includes a breakdown of all the extra stuff packed in alongside this version of the game. This includes the digital soundtrack, three-days of early-access to the game, and the story prologue. It'll also include the Aftermath post-launch DLC too, with its dedicated campaign and new playable faction.

Now, ever since the Aftermath DLC was announced, people have speculated it would be chaos-focused. The design of the DLC logo is black with a gold trim, an often-used colour scheme for the faction. However, which sort of Chaos was left up to debate. That is, until this trailer, where the answer is seemingly given away with a cheeky tease.

In its final few seconds, the trailer shows a pair of glowing yellow mechanical eyes peering out from a gloomy background. This was quickly identified as almost-certainly Vashtorr the Arkifane, a relatively new addition to Warhammer 40,000 and a fan-favourite baddie all around.

Vashtorr as a character has been getting a lot of love ever since his introduction in 2023. It was then, during the Arks of Omen campaign for the tabletop game, that he played a central part in the narrative event bridging the game's 10th and 11th edition. Since then he was the main antagonist of Boltgun 2, and was central in the 2025 novel Achmagos.

What this means for Dawn of War 4 is that, if he is a commander of Chaos forces, expect a lot of machinery and demon engines on his side. That's kind of his whole deal. Whether that means he's paired with tech-focused Dark Mechanicum as a sort of mirror to the Adeptus Mechanicus faction already in the game, or if he'll come alongside Chaos Space Marines to better reflect the Dark Angels / Blood Ravens remains to be seen. It could also be a mix of both! We'll have to wait and see.

#3758. Ex-Respawn studio Gravity Well announces "hibernation" following previous failure to secure funding and layoffs, but insists "we still believe in the IP and game we were building"

Following a round of layoffs last month that resulted in the loss of 40 jobs, which itself came after a previous source of funding pulled out in the Spring, independent studio Gravity Well has now announced that it is going into "hibernation" for the foreseeable future. The team was largely made up of devs who'd left Titanfall and Apex Legends studio Respawn Entertainment, and under the Gravity Well banner had been working on a new, still-unannounced game for around six years.

A statement posted to the main page on Gravity Well's site reads:

"We don’t exactly know what is next for us or Gravity Well, but we do know we still believe in the IP and game we were building. Even moreso, the team we managed to cultivate was truly world class and we’re going to miss getting to work with them every day. If you’re a hiring manager or recruiter and a Gravity Well resume hits your desk they come with our highest recommendation.

If you’re a publisher or investor and are interested in talking, let's connect!"

The message is signed off by its founders Drew McCoy, Jon 'Slothy' Shiring and Mon Saetern. Besides being the second project led by former Respawn developers to be doomed this year - see also Wildlight's Highguard - it's unfortunately another case of a studio made up of developers with incredible pedigrees being left at the whim of funding accruement in the current state of the industry. That said, it is noteworthy that the team have not shown anything publicly in the six years since their formation, minus a few pieces of concept art which can now be seen on its site. It's still unknown exactly what Gravity Well was working on, but it's likely to have been some kind of movement-based shooter, if the teams' experience on Titanfall, Apex Legends and Call of Duty is anything to go by. Solidarity to all affected, who I hope can find work elsewhere in the industry.

After appearing in both God of War Ragnarok and next year's God of War Laufey, Deborah Ann Woll is about to reprise her role as Faye in Amazon Prime Video's upcoming live-action series.

Variety reports that the God of War cast list is now welcoming a second actor pulled straight from Sony Santa Monica's video game series. Deborah Ann Woll first showed up in the games as Kratos' wife and Atreus' mother during God of War Ragnarok, but she's also about to enter the spotlight proper in God of War Laufey.

Amazon's God of War cast now includes Dave Bautista (Guardians of the Galaxy) as god killer Kratos, Callum Vinson (Chucky) as Atreus, Mandy Patinkin as Odin and Ólafur Darri Ólafsson as Thor. Alastair Duncan is also making the game-to-show jump by stepping back into the figurative shoes of chatty head Mimir.

Earlier in the year, the God of War show halted production when former Kratos actor Ryan Hurst suffered an on-set injury. Bautista soon took over the role and production began again in October - all of Hurst's scenes had to be reshot, of course.

There's no release date yet for the show, but it's said to follow the Norse era of the games which began in 2018's more serious and stern revamp. Amazon ordered a two-season run for the show, which apparently means both seasons will be filmed back-to-back.

Meanwhile, God of War Laufey was recently delayed from February 2027 to May 2027, giving the PS5 exclusive slightly more breathing room away from Fable, Persona 4 Revival and Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis.

"We will make the most of each moment until then by putting in the finishing touches and pushing the game to its fullest potential," developer Sony Santa Monica said at the time. "On behalf of everyone on the team, we appreciate your patience and we'll be back to share more updates soon."

While the game puts Faye in the leading role as she battles with gods in a multi-mythological afterlife, the studio was quick to note that her journey isn't considered a side game. God of War Laufey will still connect to future games in the series and, yep, Kratos will eventually be back, too.

"Genuinely, I thought I was going to be much more offended by it, but one, I'm not on social media, so that helps, and two, I don't know, I feel totally unbothered," Woll said of the online trolls who were targeting Laufey after its reveal this summer. "Because I just know it's great. It's okay if it's not your cup of tea, but in no universe is it bad."

Rockstar recreated an embarrassing mishap in Florida infrastructure.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

When you're exploring a world as realistic and well-observed as GTA 6's Leonida, it's rare for a piece of benign infrastructure to stick out. But on night one of my playthrough, I clocked some weird streetlights.

A stylistic choice by Rockstar? Maybe, but it's awfully specific, and I had a feeling there was a deeper intention behind it. So I DMed my buddy Henry, an honest-to-god Floridian who was also playing GTA 6, and asked what's up. At first he thought strange streetlights in the Key Lento area of the map were special lights meant to not disorient turtles, but those are typically red, so probably not. And that doesn't explain the purple ones.

So Henry reached out to friends in south Florida, the region that Leonida's biggest cities are based on, and they cracked the case wide open.

"The purple [lights] are definitely real. We have a ton of them down here because whoever is in charge of that in the government bought a bunch of defective lights," the anonymous Floridian responded.

Yes, actual Florida cities are lit by these dubiously dim, yet undeniably cool purple lamps. According to ClickOrlando, residents first started reporting the purple streetlights in 2023. They put up hundreds of these things across the state before they started malfunctioning—it was such a kerfuffle that the government eventually released a statement saying their vendor really screwed the pooch.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Apparently the cause was a "spectral shift caused by phosphor displacement," which essentially means the LED lights were always blue, but the coating that was supposed to make appear yellow or white or whatever didn't work. The powers that be said the malfunctioning lights would be replaced, but judging by our own sources in the state, they haven't gotten them all.

So that's fun. If you already heard about this somewhere (other than your Floridian friend), it's probably because YouTuber AnyAustin also clocked these lights in his video published yesterday. Glad I'm not the only one who couldn't resist this rabbit hole.

I like how Rockstar didn't go overboard with these lights—just like the genuine article, they're in and around parts of Leonida, but not everywhere. I'm still not sure how to explain the turquoise ones, though. A lot of local news, Reddit, and YouTube skimming did not produce a clear answer, other than other cities in America that do have green streetlights sometimes. Perhaps Key Lento has lamps busted in a slightly different way, or it's just a calming shade of blue that Rockstar thought looked nice. It does, to be fair.

#3753. Valve push on with their Steam improvements by revamping the Community Market home page and adding a watchlist to it so you're bookmarks will be a lot lighter

Another day, another Steam update! Earlier this year, Valve made some tweaks to Steam's Community Market as part of their ongoing widening of the digital storefront. The maybe Half-Life 3 developer is back with another update for the Community Market, once again bringing some fresh UI/UX bits, as well as some quality of life adjustments that should make it a bit nicer to use.

For starters, there's a new Market home page! "We've rebuilt the Market Home to load faster and present you with the most relevant items from your games," a blog post explains. "Instead of the Popular Items section, which was a small and static slice of millions of items, Trending Items will give you a glimpse into what’s new in the games you’re currently playing. The game links move up to the top spot and are now personalized, so rather than a flat and unchanging list, you get quick access to the items you're most likely to be interested in."

Next up in the update is the addition of a watchlist feature. Before, if you wanted to follow a number of items in the marketplace you'd need to bookmark everything, but now you can just save things to your watchlist; this includes the likes of specific listings, particular item types with any filters you've applied, and even specific searches, again with filters and search text. You can also apply custom names to watchlist entries in case two of them end up looking particularly similar.

There were a few other smaller bits to this update too. You'll find a new section that highlights Steam community items, i.e. trading cards and emotes, from games you've played. If you have anything listed on the marketplace, you can now change the price without having to relist it. There's a list view option while browsing items. And market pages now load faster and are more responsive. A convenient sounding update for the Steam Community Market connoisseur! Which is already live, by the way.

#3751. "That philosophy has not changed for us because of GTA 6": CD Projekt Red are staying the course on The Witcher 4 and Cyberpunk 2 after Rockstar's smash success

"We have certain ambitions when it comes to [The Witcher 4 and] Cyberpunk 2"

For publicly traded game developers, there is surely one question, with all manner of variations, that will surely be coming up again and again over the next few months: what impact will GTA 6 have on your games? CD Projekt Red were subjected to such questioning in their latest earnings call, part of which was related to sales figures of The Witcher 3 and Cyberpunk 2077, that boring kind of thing. But CEO Michal Nowakowski did also respond to a comment about how GTA 6 may affect the development of The Witcher 4 and Cyberpunk 2.

"We have certain ambitions when it comes to [The Witcher 4 and] Cyberpunk 2, they have not changed when it comes to GTA 6," Nowakowski quite plainly explains in response to a question about how the biggest game of the year may influence budget or design, already sounding just that little bit exasperated over the questions related to Rockstar's latest. "If anything happened as a result of GTA 6, it's always great to see games like that because they show you how much cool stuff can be done. That's for sure an inspiration in many ways for our developers. In terms of the budget, I gave a response [in an interview at] Gamescom; games The Witcher or Cyberpunk 2, although they are not GTA, are not budget-driven developments."

Nowakowski goes on to clarify that he doesn't mean this in the sense of not caring about budgets, or that they have infinite money, but noted that you "cannot make games," with solely that focus. "They are ambition-driven developments and money is important, the budgets are not indefinite, that's not what we're saying. And honestly, that philosophy has not changed for us because of GTA 6." This is obviously kind of a non-answer in one sense, but I think it does point to how GTA 6 is going to create some uncomfortable expectations for many triple-A devs when next to none of them will have Rockstar money to fulfill them.

In any case, obviously the next big thing for CD Projekt Red is The Witcher 3's Songs of the Past expansion. Still no release date attached to that one, though it's currently expected to release sometime in 2027 next year. The Witcher 4 is then slated for release not long after that in 2028, but in this day and age, I'm sure a delay would be an incredibly safe bet to make.

#3750. Activision calls Banjo-Kazooie one of its "iconic gaming franchises," raising hopes for long-awaited new game

Banjo-Kazooie - the iconic Rare platformer starring an absent-minded bear and the sassy red bird he carries in a backpack - has been on hiatus for years, but a new Activision job listing has raised hopes for a new game.

In a LinkedIn post advertising a 'Product Manager, Emergent Franchises' role, the publisher wrote that it's "home to iconic gaming franchises including Call of Duty, Crash Bandicoot, Spyro the Dragon, and now… Halo, Age of Empires, Sea of Thieves, and Banjo Kazooie."

"Become part of the team working on building, growing, and shaping many of these franchises," the listing goes on. "As a Product Manager, you will serve as the publishing product lead for an upcoming premium console & PC title, driving the product from concept to launch."

If you're scratching your brain trying to remember when Activision took control of the beloved platformer, well, it happened during Xbox's last massive internal shakeup. Amid the mass layoffs and studio divestments, Xbox also made some drastic changes to its corporate structure - Halo, World's Edge and Rare were all slotted under Activision's supervision.

Rare's 40-year history includes almost too many notable games to list, but the internal rejig presumably put Activision in control of games like Conker, Viva Pinata and Killer Instinct, alongside the aforementioned pirate hit Sea of Thieves and Banjo-Kazooie.

The job post is by no means confirmation that a new Banjo-Kazooie game is in development, but it is the only series named here that can be considered dormant, perhaps hinting that Activision has plans to revive it down the line. Crash Bandicoot 4 and Spyro: A Realm Beyond lay out a pretty good blueprint for its return, I think.

The last properly new game in the series came 18 years ago with the Xbox 360's Banjo-Kazooie: Nuts and Bolts, a surprisingly good physics-driven vehicle construction sandbox.

Since then, Banjo and Kazooie showed up as a playable fighter in Super Smash Bros Ultimate. More recently, a fan-made PC port and an Evercade Double Pack have kept the series chugging.

Composer Grant Kirkhope was slightly more hopeful about the prospect of a Banjo-Threeie back in September. "I do know of like three companies that have actually physically pitched to Microsoft or to Rare about making another Banjo-Kazooie game, and I don't think anyone was successful," he said at the time.

Bring on the awkward dinner table conversations.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

I can’t remember the last time an SNL sketch went as viral as “Sister” did a week ago. While impressions, “Weekend Update” and host and musical guest moments are topics of conversation at Studio 8h every week, everyone and their mother saw the “Sister” sketch, and now all those people are going to be in a confined space with one another over Thanksgiving weekend. The comment section is all over this awkwardness.

I’d already been thinking about “Sister” ahead of my own Thanksgiving celebration. Caretaking has hit my family hard while my mom’s battled cancer twice, and while I have another sister who has helped me with those dynamics, SNL’s John Mulaney sketch really spoke to me, and I just already know it’s going to come up at Thanksgiving for many families dealing with caring for an older family member. For us, it should be a humorous conversation. For many? Not so much.

Written by Chase Rosenberg, Mikey Day, Streeter Seidell, and Simon Rich, the sketch follows brothers who have implemented their “sister” for elder care, and have then stepped back to let her handle everything that comes with that label. It’s really funny, but there are also many rings of truth to it, and it has sparked a lot of conversation from angry siblings who feel burnt out and tasked with doing too much. It's led to so much discourse in the days after its release, I'd imagine it will land on the list of Saturday Night Live sketches we'll talk about for years.

Now, one Internet user thinks it’s going to be a big topic of conversation over the holidays, and many SNL viewers agree the timing was probably intentional for a sketch that was this biting and led to so many personal feelings.

Streeter Seidell dedicated the sketch to his own sister Heidi! I wonder how many awkward moments this will inspire next Thursday. 😂

In fact, lots of people think the timing of the SNL sketch was perfect or awful, depending on what you think about it. I don't want to harp too hard

One viral tweet also noted the release of the sketch just before family get togethers had to be “deliberate." (Again, it's definitely interesting.)

SNL gets a bad rap, often deservedly so. But this is a sketch we'll be talking about for decades. Look at the replies and quote-tweets: person after person after person saying "this is my life", or "I'm Sister." Dropping this right before Thanksgiving had to be deliberate, right?

To note, I don't personally agree with the bent that SNL deserves a bad rap. The show has had ups and downs as long as I've watched it, and silly bits can sometimes drive home harder than some of the political or Update stuff. While not on topic to Thanksgiving like the Adele-themed "Thanksgiving Miracle" sketch with Aidy Bryant, I do think this is one we will continue to watch and discuss this week.

I'd just recommend people do so before people are too hyped up on tryptophan, alcohol and sugar.

The Muv-Luv trilogy is a visual novel phenomenon that's tough to explain. The first game's a schlocky high school romance generally considered a chore to get through before the good stuff, when the protagonist of that story finds himself out of his depth as a mecha pilot fighting aliens in an apocalyptic warzone. It becomes a dense, twisty, and increasingly serious saga that just happens to star a dropkick hero right out of a harem anime.

Muv-Luv's popular enough to have a bunch of spin-offs, the latest being a gacha game called Muv-Luv Girls Garden in which you collect girls to pilot mecha in automated battles, and of course said girls are romanceable. This caused a problem, as players discovered when they made it to some of the adult scenes only to find dialogue in which characters repeated at each other, "I can't provide a translation for explicit sexual content."

Yeah, Muv-Luv Girls Garden was translated into English with AI. The Steam page does mention this in its AI-generated content disclosure, though hilariously it does so in untranslated Japanese: "1部ローカライズに生成AIを使用しています。"

Players are unimpressed, with the Steam user rating dropping to Mostly Negative. As one user review puts it, "What if you want to goon But God says I'm unable to provide a translation for this text because it contains explicit sexual content."

Other user reviews complain about changes to the original artwork, with characters having accessories like teddy bears and hair ribbons taken away, as well as being given larger breasts or made to look taller. It's tougher to emphasize with players who are mad that characters in an adult game have been changed to look less like 12-year-olds, especially given the pressure put on Valve by payment processors to remove certain kinds of games from Steam.

#3747. Bare fist, megastructure climbing roguelike White Knuckle gets its penultimate region in The Core, a sterile, hostile reactor sector that you'll probably die in

Hope you've been training your grip strength

The beauty of stepping into a digital world is that it allows me to accomplish things I couldn't possibly dream of doing in the real one, like, say, climbing anything that's higher than your average step ladder. White Knuckle is one such game that's all about playing around with uncomfortable heights, and a new update for the early access roguelike went live this week introducing a new, hostile environment: The Core.

The sixth region to be added to the game, and the "penultimate challenge," implying that there's just one more area to come after this one, The Core takes you to Habitation Blue's reactor sector. "Use everything you have available to fight through the now Mass-controlled Superstructure Automated Processing System (SAPS) and her array of mechanized defenses," explains a Steam news post. "The Core is the sterile power station of the Superstructure, a massive network of coolant lines, offices, catwalks, and more, all of which is highly secured by an army of turrets, drones, and androids. Even without the Mass hot on your tail it would not be easy to escape."

There are a few new subregions to be found too, of course, but more importantly a new major artifact. It's called The Scissors, and with it you cut off your hands ("yes, really") to "gain a spectral form that increases your reach, hand stamina, and damage," while using the artifact. You can also throw the scissors like a boomerang to hurt enemies from afar, and "killing enemies also counts as eating if using Survival Mode binding, or the perks Conditioned Polyphagia & Unstoppable Conviction."

Beyond this there's a selection of new weapons, like the piton crossbow which shoots "pitons at range, to set up routes and to deal extreme damage." The pulse pump is a new trinket that introduces a chargeable mid-air jump. There's new perks like one called nest egg, where you gain a "second major artifact at the start of the Nest, at the cost of halving all roach deposits in your run." Previous regions have also received some new room tiles, and there's a few fresh cosmetics to pick up too. There's some secret thing to find in this update as well, "but you'll need to play to find out…" Hop to it, I guess!

"Unlike every other chapter, I actually feel like I know what I'm doing this time."

Toby Fox has given eager fans an update on the development of Deltarune Chapter 6 and Chapter 7 - the Undertale follow-up's final two episodes.

"Chapte 6 is progressing well," he wrote in a new blog post. "The game is now a structurally complete draft that can be played from the beginning to the end. All the maps, events, and battles exist. (Although there's still one optional event which is dragging out a bit…)"

While the bones are supposedly all there, Fox explained that he and his team still need to knock out localisation, testing and polishing. "Much of the game looks complete… but, some important scenes and details are still undercooked in their presentation, so it's going to take a bit longer before we can really move to full-on testing."

Deltarune Chapter 6 was previously described as a slightly shorter episode that should hopefully set up the game's finale quite nicely. Despite being on the smaller side, Fox said he understandably doesn't want to rush development and "would like it to be as good as possible."

And since Deltarune's next chapter is almost past the finish line - at least, in some respect - that means certain members of the team have already moved over to Chapter 7.

"Well, we've only just started," Fox continued. "I read out the events and dialogue of Chapter 7 to the team. However, just when the story reached a critical moment, I stopped reading… I told my team they need to complete more of the game before I tell them what happens. Everyone agrees it's more fun this way"

"Unlike every other Chapter, I actually feel like I know what I'm doing this time, so I have a lot of confidence."

Deltarune's been on a long journey to get here, but, thankfully, the end is finally in sight. Deltarune debuted as a free download all the way back in 2018, a second chapter then dropped in 2021, the next two launched together four years later, before the arrival of the most recent Chapter 5 this year.

We don't know exactly how long Deltarune's last two chapters might take, but the good news is that it's already been a pretty fantastic game for years. Here's hoping those loose threads don't dangle for much longer.

#3744. Modders already have GTA 6 running on PC, after CyberLeek released a full Xbox build of the game

A PC version of Grand Theft Auto 6 - one from unofficial sources, at least - may be closer than we thought. After suddenly returning last week with a near-full build of the Xbox version, notorious leaker CyberLeek has now posted the missing piece they intentionally held back: the game's executable (.exe) file.

"The exe is out. Always free. An early Christmas gift from CL," CyberLeek reportedly wrote, as relayed on Reddit. "The torch passes to the open source re-comp and emulation projects."

Hours later, the recompilation modders and hackers part of the Project Leonida Discord server - the current hub for all GTA 6 recompilation efforts - posted footage of the game booting up on PC.

In just a matter of hours, modders - with the help of Claude AI - managed to turn the leaked Xbox build into a PC port, of sorts. In this Reddit video, you can see the game boot up to the initial setup before hitting a black screen. The build is clearly not yet playable, though Eurogamer has not directly verified those claims.

Shayder, one of the lead developers on Project Leonida, said in a since-deleted post on X that we should "expect a lot of static recompilation work to be done soon." On the project's Discord server, they later clarified that it could take about a week for the build to reach a playable state on PC.

As for CyberLeek, the leaker is still soliciting donations for a secret project "for the gamers", adding in the build's readme file, "Nobody has to give anything, and every release stays free either way. But every donation is a vote for more of this, and so is every trade of the token."

Rockstar has not announced a PC version of GTA 6, but the company has historically released its games on PC several months after their console debut. In October, a report said GTA 6's PC version would arrive in the first quarter of 2027, an unusually short gap between the console and PC releases.

These latest recompilation efforts, however, may force Rockstar to speed up development of the PC version. Though the recompiled build may never reach the level of quality or stability of an official port, many of those eager to play the game on PC likely wouldn't care.

#3743. Bitmap Brothers' iconic, robotic RTS game Z is unofficially back thanks to an open source, 3D remake

There can be such a wonderful charm that comes from fan games because the people that make them really are just in it for the love of the (literal) game. They ain't gonna make any money from this thing! So I'm quite tickled by OpenZ, a 3D remake of the 1996 RTS game Z from The Bitmap Brothers that's completely open source (and, thankfully, hand made).

As it currently stands, OpenZ is a one-person operation who's remaking the game to celebrate its 30th anniversary. "This is the faithful 3D remake we always wanted but never got. Every single detail has been meticulously recreated and restored with an almost ridiculous level of attention," explains the game's itch.io page. "OpenZ is completely free and open source. It will never be sold: no donations, no commercial use, ever. All assets are 100% original, and no copyrighted material from the original game is used."

At the moment there's only two levels, though it's sounding like it's the full run of them, described as having been "meticulously restored and polished to an extreme level of detail," with some added improvements thanks to "30 years of RTS game design experience." There's a few new bits to find in this remake too, like new mech and electrobot units.

It sounds like there are bigger plans for the remake overall, presumably for the full game too: "This is only the beginning. Together as a community we can bring Z back to its former glory: more restored classic levels, completely original new levels, new units and maybe even multiplayer." As mentioned, it's completely free to download and play too, so where's the harm in giving it a go!

Even the original Dark Lord himself has the Pattinson Jokes.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Robert Pattinson was just announced as the next James Bond, and the internet has spent the days since joking that no Hollywood role is safe from him. I thought those jokes had about run their course until Ralph Fiennes weighed in. The actor who terrified an entire generation of Harry Potter fans as Lord Voldemort was asked who should take over the role in HBO's upcoming television series, and his answer was so dry that I almost missed how funny it was.

Fiennes was speaking with the Associated Press at the New York premiere of The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping on Nov. 16. The conversation turned to the new book-to-screen adaptation of the Harry Potter novels and whether he'd consider returning as He Who Must Not Be Named. Fiennes indicated he'd had his fill of the character. As for who should put on the robes next, he offered one name:

Maybe they'll offer it to Robert Pattinson.

I love how little effort went into that joke. The Red Dragon veteran actor didn't need to explain it, either. Following Pattinson's Bond casting, social media has been having a field day with the idea that he's taking every acting job. One popular variation suggests that artificial intelligence isn't coming for anyone's job because Pattinson will get there first. The OG Potter villain apparently decided to throw one more highly coveted part onto the pile.

Of course, there's another reason his suggestion is particularly good, and it involves a Harry Potter movie I still have a hard time watching without getting a little upset. Pattinson played Cedric Diggory in 2005's Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire, the same film that introduced Fiennes as the fully resurrected Voldemort. Cedric made it through the Triwizard Tournament only to be murdered by Peter Pettigrew on Voldemort's orders. It's a miserable ending for one of the story's most likable characters.

So imagine the actor who played Cedric now taking over as the man who ordered his death. I'd almost pay to see Pattinson in the makeup just for that bit of full-circle casting, although I'm pretty sure Fiennes was having a laugh rather than making a serious recommendation.

The two actors also have a second franchise connection thanks to Bond. Fiennes played M opposite Daniel Craig in Skyfall, Spectre and No Time to Die, so he's watched a different actor occupy the 007 role that Pattinson is now inheriting. The Tenet actor has already spent plenty of time bouncing between massive franchises, from Twilight to The Batman. It's getting hard to name an iconic fictional universe he hasn't visited.

The actual casting of Voldemort remains a mystery. Fiennes previously said he was all for Cillian Murphy playing the Dark Lord, and there's been no shortage of rumors about who might portray the villain. He's also offered the eventual actor some practical advice on navigating Voldemort's robes. Whoever gets the job has quite a performance to follow.

I'm excited to see who HBO chooses, but Fiennes has made me realize there's one more possibility I hadn't considered. If Pattinson somehow lands the role, he'll have played Cedric Diggory and the wizard who had him killed. At this rate, I'd hesitate to rule out anything.

You can revisit Fiennes' take on Voldemort, or the eight films of the original Harry Potter film franchise, streaming with your HBO Max subscription.

#3741. Microsoft reportedly looked into killing paid multiplayer for next-gen Xbox Helix consoles

A new report from Windows Central details how Xbox was reportedly looking into removing the paywall that prevents players without Xbox Live from playing online games, only to potentially renege on its decision sometime during production of the next-gen device.

"Sources close to Microsoft's plans tell me Xbox Helix was originally conceived as a true console-PC hybrid with access to Windows PC games and stores such as Steam, alongside another major change: no paywall for online multiplayer," says the Windows Central report. It goes on to note that this Xbox Live-free plan was iterated upon under Xbox's previous leadership, but with Asha Sharma's appointment as Xbox head in February, all that apparently changed. I guess she did promise "radically different business models", after all.

The revised plan has reportedly been altered thanks to a myriad of factors affecting the Xbox business: new management, rising component costs, and a shifting hardware strategy, are all outlined specifically in the report. We've previously heard that Xbox's next-gen console could cost up to $1,800, with a handheld version coming in 2027 and a full release by holiday 2028 (a Helix console at $1,200 would mean a 50 percent increase on top of Series X's current price, for what it's worth). Sharma has stressed Helix will launch as "a family of devices" that will act as a bridge between PC and Xbox capable of playing games from both platforms.

If Xbox has, indeed, decided to scrap the idea of free online multiplayer access, it'll be a blow to the idealistic 'PC and Xbox' platform that Microsoft has been touting for the past few years: PC players do not need a subscription in order to access online modes, so - right out the gate - there will be a division between one group of players and the other. Perhaps this is why we've heard a little change in the tone of how Sharma and other Xbox bosses are talking about Helix more recently - these hints that the console will be a true PC-and-console hybrid have died down, and been replaced by insinuations that we'll see more of a traditional console with the "ability to play your PC games."

Xbox has been running Xbox Live as a service since 2002, when it launched on the original Xbox console. By 2005, it was split into gold and silver tiers to distinguish free players from those that paid. In 2023, the service was fully renamed Xbox Game Pass Core, looping in access to the base roster of Game Pass games with online play.

Catch Port Gellhorn's creepy serial killer and end the 20-year mystery.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The GTA 6 Missing Persons case is available as early as Chapter 1, but you'll need access to both Lucia and Jason to wrap up the side quest in Chapter 2. Your stint as a fledgling detective begins in an abandoned warehouse near Mo's shop in Gellhorn, though there are two ways to flag the objective on your map and start the hunt for Gellhorn's serial killer.

If you begin in Chapter 1 when you can only play as Jason, head straight to the abandoned warehouse to begin. This is how I began the quest the first time, after following a pack of coyotes through a small opening on the side of the abandoned warehouse. This route gives you an extra text conversation where Jason sends Lucia creepy photos from the warehouse.

Begin in Chapter 2 by heading to the Starlet Motel lobby in Gellhorn and inspecting the missing persons posters. Afterward, head to the abandoned warehouse as a couple or go alone, and squeeze through the crawl space.

After crawling inside the warehouse, walk to the far end and turn right to enter the glowing red room. Go a little farther to find the, uh, "trophies," and inspect all three lockers, along with the missing persons posters on the wall. This is where you begin your hunt for Gellhorn's three missing tourists.

I've got all three locations highlighted below, but if you want to solve it yourself, now is the time to turn back.

The first missing person in northwest Gellhorn is in an abandoned trailer—the water tower's shadow is your giveaway. Run along the fence and enter the blue building from the back. There's an awfully suspicious hole in the floor, so pull the remaining floorboards back to discover what's left of Patrick Murray.

Call the Kelly County Tip Line after you find Patrick's remains and leave a message. No one will answer the phone, for now.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

The second missing person is in the junkyard, inside the trunk of an old pink DeVanity. The junkyard is right beside Pay 'n' Spray off Gellhorn Ave, across the street from the drive-in theatre. You'll spot Susanne Keeble's pink car with the PRTYGRL license plate while facing the drive-in.

After finding a second body, call the tip line again to finally speak to an investigator. They're thrilled to hear there's renewed interest in the case, and ask that you keep in contact should you make any further discoveries.

The third missing person is in a U-shaped inlet off the Borrachero Sound. You can find the smaller body of water by traveling southeast from the Wild Hog Point hangar. The view of Wild Hog Point from the tree in the creepy photo is your giveaway, so start looking for a submerged car when you find the right perspective.

After finding a third body, the investigator from the tip line asks to meet in the abandoned warehouse. And no, it's not just you, it's a pretty shady proposition.

When you're ready for the meeting, consider whether you want to go with your partner or go alone. Both seem to give me the same boost to Jason and Lucia's relationship status, elevating it to Hot Together (4/4) status for the first time in Chapter 2. It had dropped all the way down to Partners in Crime (2/4) just before this, so the Missing Persons quest was a much-appreciated bump.

You can also get the serial killer's glasses from his body if you choose to continue as a couple. They're beyond creepy, so I wouldn't blame you if you left them there, but aside from that, there's no cash reward. You will have to do it, though, if you're going for a 100% GTA 6 run.

As either Jason or Lucia, return to the abandoned warehouse trophy room and meet Alvan West—the man you spoke to on the Kelly County Tips Line. He's got a 'surprise' waiting for you in the fourth locker, and a fight ensues after checking it out.

Going alone means there's no one there to save the passed out Jason or Lucia, and the serial killer takes them to a cave in Lummox County. The attack automatically triggers a character swap, leaving you to investigate your partner's whereabouts after receiving suspicious texts.

Enter the abandoned warehouse trophy room just like before while your partner waits outside. When they sense something is off, they'll run inside to save you just as you pass out. After Alvan is dead, inspect his body—you can take his glasses as a souvenir. That's freak behavior, but I'm not judging. We gotta get that 100% cosmetic collection somehow.

"Grats to everyone who got Exalted already"

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

World of Warcraft: Forever just got some brand-new changes that finally address the Alterac Valley shenanigans making rounds online – finally forcing players to, you know, engage with the actual PvP part of PvP.

In case you're out of the loop, the Alterac Valley is essentially a massive battleground in which the Alliance and Horde fight over control – you know, basic PvP stuff. Ultimately, you win by killing the enemy general. So, what are those "shenanigans" I mentioned? Well, players have turned the area into a reputation-farming hotspot rather than a true battleground, running straight to the general and ignoring everything else.

They've worked out that losing quickly is an efficient way to farm reputation, too, when compared to engaging in a more lengthy, competitive match. Reputation gets folks some very nice equipment, including pre-raid gear, after all. People who care about PvP and not just exploiting Blizzard's balance issues haven't exactly been pleased, though – and that's where those changes I touched on earlier come in.

You'll find the full details on the studio's official forums, where the developers start by going over their own observations: "We've seen that players in Alterac Valley were frequently completing the battleground without capturing the objectives, so we've made some adjustments to incentivize a focus on the objectives rather than rushing to kill the enemy faction's General." And boy, have they made adjustments indeed.

"The intent with these adjustments is for Honor gains to be relatively the same and reputation to be increased per match. Additionally, the difficulty of enemy creatures inside Alterac Valley has been lower than intended, so we've increased that, and we've made some adjustments to how the Warmasters/Marshals and Faction Generals behave to improve their sturdiness." So, what do these tweaks look like? Well, first off, and perhaps unsurprisingly, the reputation and Honor players gain from killing the enemy's general "has been significantly reduced." In turn, however, reputation gained via other objectives (graveyards, towers, and the like) and killing enemy NPCs has seen an increase. The damage dealt by enemies, as well as their health, has gone up, too, along with a few other adjustments I'd say are worth reading through.

Not everyone is pleased with the updates, though, as many feel it's too little, too late. Over on Reddit, fans discuss Blizzard's "fixes," with the top comment sarcastically remarking, "Grats to everyone who got Exalted already." A response to them adds, "Exploit early, exploit often holds true as always." Another player writes, "Sweats get to 60, take a massive leap even further from 10 different exploits/bugs, and then the ladder is pulled up. Feels so good."

Yeah… it really does not feel good, I'm guessing, to see others benefit from a debatable exploit only for devs to later patch it out. Hopefully, Blizzard's a bit quicker about things next time – but it's at least clear the team is listening. This isn't the first time it's responded to complaints in WoW: Forever, either. Just recently, devs took aim at gold exploiters, striking down one of the MMO's most infamous streamers in the process.

Some of these artists played a significant role in the game. Justice, for example, helped compose the game's original soundtrack and several of their tracks appear throughout the game. There are others, too.

Both Sexyy Red and Denzel Curry voice characters in the game's later chapters. Others like Kodack Black and Freddie Gibbs also show up, too - that's not to mention the huge number of musicians who make an appearance in the game's many radio stations. If you listen through those, you'll hear the voices of Keith Richards, Lana Del Ray, The Alchemist and others.

Musical talent also played an additional role in creating the TV advertisements and shows you can watch in the game. Zack Fox is one example, as is Weird Al Yankovic. Both wrote parts of the game's enticing and absurd big screen entertainment - which makes sense given the pair's shared comedy background.

If you're playing through the game right now, you may benefit from Eurogamer's GTA 6 walkthrough, as well as the full list of GTA 6 cheats.

#3737. I'm not smart enough for the blocky, Factorio-esque spaceship and -station building sim Astario, but now that it's out in early access maybe you could be

There are many different kinds of smarts, and the kind of smarts I am are absolutely zero help when it comes to games like Astario, a spaceship and space station building factory sim reminiscent of Factorio that just launched into early access. I think there's just so many moving parts in ways I can't wrap my head around, but I'm fairly confident that some of you will be, so I'll try to use the smarts I do have to tell you about it a bit more.

Astario puts you in a spaceship in, uh, space, and oh what a big space it is. I have no idea if it's a to scale universe or anything, but it certainly looks quite expansive. There is a Minecraftian quality to it in that you must fly about and find resources from things like asteroids and other bits of technological scrap, all of which is divided up into blocks. You can get quite granular with it, inspecting each individual cube up close to see if it's a material that you can make use of, adding it to your haul for use elsewhere.

As you acquire different kinds of blocks, be they functional or structural, you can build up various new vehicles and "create an imposing machine where all components work together to achieve your goal. Plan or design your build out of armor blocks, power supplies, life support components, tools, and production machinery. Construct an orbital station with a stash of cargo containers, or anchor your production base to an asteroid and turn its ores into more blocks, fully automatically. Equip your ship with docking ports for refueling or recharging." How you build things is up to you, you've seemingly got a lot of free reign in terms of artistic expression.

And then of course there's bits of production machinery you can produce that in turn net you recipes and the like so you can continue to improve your ship or space stations. "All production blocks have input and output ports that can be automated using logistic pipes which use request-based item routing," explains the game's Steam page of how techy you can get with it. "Simply hook up your inputs to a cargo container, and the machine will pull what it needs. Mining can be temporarily automated using specialized drills, which mine until the resources within its scope are depleted." If any of this sounds like it's up your alley, then you can pick up Astario on Steam in early access now.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The Marvel Cinematic Universe is always expanding, and fans who spent years watching the Marvel movies in order are counting down the days until Avengers: Doomsday hits theaters in December. Anticipation is high for the upcoming Marvel movie, especially because Doomsday's cast list includes entire teams of superheroes. That includes Channing Tatum's Gambit, who is clarifying comments about toning down his character's accent.

What we know about Avengers: Doomsday is limited, but Tatum finally gets the chance to join the X-Men in the blockbuster. Gambit's accent was fodder for jokes in Deadpool & Wolverine, with the other characters not being able to understand him. Although in an interview from The Associated Press' Instagram, he weighed in on chatter he'd be toning it down for the next Marvel blockbuster. In his words:

I think I've been quoted in the press about toning down the accent. That is not exactly what I'm doing. I'm just speaking less Cajun French.

Honestly, this tracks. Tatum's Doomsday Dunkin' Ad featured him with Gambit's signature accent, and it was easy enough to understand the mutant as he spoke to H.E.R.B.I.E. about the coffee company's seasonal treats. He's still going to be using the Cajun dialect, but won't be going so far as to use Cajun French throughout the course of the Avengers movie's runtime.

Later in the same interview, the Magic Mike icon went on to speak about the difference between the Cajun accent and Cajun French. In the 46 year-old actor's words:

It's hard to explain, but basically Cajun French is French that almost French people can't even understand. So I'm speaking less of that, but the Cajun accent's still there.

There you have it. Fans shouldn't expect Tatum to sound THAT much different than he did in Deadpool & Wolverine (which is streaming with a Disney+ subscription). He'll be using the same dialect, but won't be veering into French at all throughout the blockbuster. As such, the other heroes he interacts with will presumably be able to understand him.

The final trailer for Avengers: Doomsday showed a bit more of Tatum's Gambit in battle, and his kinetic abilities look like they're going to be awesome in the movie's action sequences. We've seen him going to blows with Simu Liu's Shang-Chi, but it looks like he'll eventually work alongside The Avengers against Doctor Doom and his army of Sentinels.

Fans have been waiting a long time to see the card-throwing mutant take center stage, especially since Tatum was attached to a Gambit movie for years that sat in development hell. He's finally in the role, albeit under different circumstances.

Avengers: Doomsday will hit theaters on December 18th as part of the 2026 movie release list. The stakes are high for the blockbuster, and I'm curious to see how many characters fall in the forthcoming battle.

#3735. AI-generated GTA 6 PC ports get nuked in alleged Rockstar takedown spree, as former Bungie dev hails "most ridiculous dumpster fire ever"

3007 Github repos allegedly DMCA'd at a stroke

One of the creators of an unofficial AI-generated PC "port" of Grand Theft Auto 6 claims that Rockstar and Take-Two Interactive have already stepped in to shut down the project, though the fearful work of slop-and-pasting GTA 6 to PC appears to be continuing in other hands. Titled "Leonida", after the game's setting, the port is a recompilation – that is, a translation of the game's original code into code that'll run natively on different hardware, rather than being live translated by an emulator as you play. It's based on an incomplete GTA 6 Xbox build of the game, including the all-important executable file, which was leaked earlier in the week by crypto grifter Cyberleek.

As documented by former Bungie developer Amy Hendricks in an increasingly depressed Bluesky thread (excerpt: "This is the most ridiculous dumpster fire ever"), Leonida is or was being made using Claude and Google's Antigravity tools. Going by Hendricks's posts, which are based on watching a Leonida stream, much of the recomp's creation seems to have consisted of one or more high school kids typing prompts like "work faster", while spending hundreds or thousands of dollars in usage fees.

The Leonida team appear to have succeeded in getting the game to boot on PC, but two key members, NotRexed and Shayder, have now withdrawn from the project and scrubbed any mention of it from their social media feeds.

In posts preserved by cheery RPS fanzine PCGamer, NotRexed shared a snapshot of a copyright infringement takedown notification from Discord. They explained their decision to call it quits as follows: "Rockstar taking my server down was only part of the reason. Like I’ve said before, I’m a 15 year old kid. Managing school and sports is hard enough without having middle aged men yell and complain to you on Discord." I myself am a middle aged man, but don't despair, NotRexed! I am not going to yell at you. I am simply going to reach for a moderately small violin.

As reported by PCG, the Leonida Discord server has now been shut down, and the Github repository for the recompilation's code has been nuked. Hendricks has shared an alleged takedown request from a representative of Take-Two Interactive, according to which Github have taken action against 3,007 forks (that is, duplicates for the purposes of making a separate version) from the original Leonida repo. Meanwhile, somebody has set up a leaderboard to chart the progress of several other GTA 6 recomp projects. I'm sure Take-Two's IP enforcement teams appreciate their efforts.

A few days prior to GTA 6's release on console last week, Rockstar North's former tech director Obbe Vermeij told RPS that the GTA makers would release the PC version sooner than anticipated to avoid losing any cash to generative AI rip-offs. IGN subsequently asked Take-Two's CEO Strauss Zelnick for his thoughts on this. Zelnick replied that the company are "not in the least cavalier" about the risk, but are confident people would rather play the game as Rockstar intended.

#3734. More than 39 million people have played GTA 6 on PlayStation alone, Sony says, as the game breaks all-time player numbers on the platform

Sony's revealed staggering statistics relating to the popularity of Grand Theft Auto on PlayStation 5, not least that more than 39 million unique people have played the game there. That's more than the official GTA 6 day-one sales tally of 32.5m copies across all platforms.

Unsurprisingly, with such massive numbers, GTA 6 is a record-breaker on PlayStation. According to the PlayStation Blog, the game has recorded the highest number of concurrent players on PlayStation ever, surpassing any previous record across all kinds of game - multiplayer, free-to-play and single-player.

In addition, PlayStation also saw "the largest number of newly connected PS5 consoles on a single day" since the console's launch, outside of end-of-year holidays, suggesting that Rockstar's latest game, more than any other PS5 game released so far, has driven hardware sales. GTA 6 is apparently the first game played on 70 percent of new PS5 consoles.

The average GTA 6 playtime, per person, is a considerable 17.4 hours, the blog says, and the total number of hours spent playing the game is 683 million - a number so high I can't contextualise it.

Microsoft hasn't announced equivalent data for Xbox but I assume the game is a record-breaker there, too, given that it broke pre-order Xbox Store records in the same way GTA 6 did on PlayStation. However, GTA 6 is estimated to have sold far more copies on PlayStation - as many as 75 percent of its total sales, according to Alinea Analytics analyst Rhys Elliott.

Elliott estimated that GTA 6 amassed a colossal 44.9m sales by the end of its opening weekend, and that 33.7m of those were on PlayStation 5 (which still doesn't reach the '39 million unique players' stat Sony has just trotted out) and 11.2m were on Xbox. That amount of sales would earn Rockstar something like $4bn in revenue.

The arrival of GTA 6 has, then, been seismic. The game has wowed critics and dominated conversation not only in the games industry but also across entertainment news and mainstream news. Meanwhile, however, we await the verdict in the Rockstar Games employment tribunal in Scotland, relating to the sudden firing of 34 employees a year ago. Was Rockstar union-busting, as alleged? It'll be a historic ruling if deemed so.

The thing you must understand is that I'm not mad. No, really, I'm not upset at all—as a matter of fact, I'm happy for your level 60 character to complete Scarlet Subterfuge (and its follow-up, In Dreams) with less back-and-forth trekking than me. I'm chuffed for you. Really, I am.

Ahem—as you can tell by my current state of grumpiness, WoW: Forever issued a bunch of hotfixes, which I will do my due diligence in describing before I have a good moan: Alterac Valley has had some tweaks to stop people "frequently completing the battleground without capturing the objectives", balance druids have had some buffs, and some major bugs (such as hunter pets not being able to crit) have been addressed.

That last point's a bit of contention in the community, given hunters are out-performing other classes in damage, but given we're just three weeks into the game with a couple of weeks left to go before the raid tier, I'm not sweating the lack of an immediate nerf bat.

Right, there's my journalistic obligation taken care of. Here's why I'm (not) upset.

Scarlet Subterfuge—and In Dreams—is widely considered one of the crappiest quests in Classic, and given this is a game that's already rife with inconvenience—inconvenience I am usually all for—that's saying something. In it, you need to go and find Highlord Taelan Fordring, son of Tirion Fordring, and remove the scarlet-coloured wool from his eyes.

Story-wise, this quest kicks ass. You're finding the son of the guy who wielded the Ashbringer. Realising his life has been a lie, he hulks out, cleaving down his former scarlet allies, and marches out of the fortress side-by-side with you. Mechanically, it sucks so much, dude.

To reach Fordring the younger, you need to go halfway across the zone, talk to an illusionist hermit, and don a disguise. Then you need to jog all the way up to where Taelan is to give him the news.

So that means that if anybody else is doing the quest by the time you get there, you need to either:

The actual escort is annoying, too: Since Taelan can technically handle the Scarlet Crusade on his lonesome, accepted practice for this quest has been to simply let him handle things. Which both makes it take ages and makes it difficult to find a group so that you can do it the intended way.

As a cherry on top, you can't really skip this quest outright as it gives some really powerful pre-BiS endgame items. Still, I persevered, I did it yesterday, and Blizzard, uh. Blizzard gave the disguise an hour-long duration literally today.

"Western Plaguelands - The Scarlet Illusion granted during the quest 'Scarlet Subterfuge' now lasts an hour (was 30 minutes)."

This doesn't make the quest any less of a headache to finish, but hey—at least if someone else is already doing it, you won't have to jog back to your hag friend or play the log-in, log-out Hokey Pokey until he respawns. Good for you.

#3732. Delivering "a more modern Garry's Mod" is the goal of spiritual successor S&box's revamped sandbox mode, as classic GMod's workshop addon system returns

"I thought that spawning from the cloud was better...but I was wrong"

Facepunch Studios continue to work on S&box, the mix of open source game development platform and Garry's Mod spiritual successor they released to mixed reviews earlier this year. That rough start has it in need of a redemption arc, which the Rust devs are hoping will be powered by going free-to-play and making changes like the revamp of sandbox mode they've just rolled out.

"This new system isn't really new," Newman wrote. "It's the exact same system that Garry's Mod uses. I hold my hands up here, I thought that spawning from the cloud was better...but I was wrong. There definitely is something a lot nicer about installing a big model pack and then having everything right there. I'm sorry it took me so long to come around to realising this."

Similarly, in terms of the updated sandbox mode, Newman noted he feels the team have been "walking the line of making a more modern Garry's Mod really well". "I'm excited by all the possibilities of it," he continued. "Obviously there aren't a ton of addons right now but what we do have is showing a LOT of potential, and that's only going to grow. I've been going through improving things that feel outdated or stupid. I'm resisting bending it all too far, I want it to stay kind of familiar for everyone, but I think we can improve a few things in our new engine."

A number of old school sandbox props, such as chunks of robotics, wheels, gears, and hunks of steel girder are on their way back, while Facepunch are finally ready to add in water. "It has waves," Newman wrote of the latter. "The physics objects get tossed around in the waves. You can go underwater, and swim, and there's caustics and fog and particles and post process effects and stuff." Also, NPCs now "live directly in the engine" making it easier to set up a fight club.

A simplified menu and a whole bunch of performance and dev-focused tweaks round out this update, so go through the full notes if you're keen to read about the likes of workshop mounts and VRAM fragmentation.

As of writing, S&box is still yet to go free-to-play, a change Newman and co previously said is coming "towards the end of the year". If it can nail recapturing the classic GMod magic with updates that players actually want, I think it stands a chance of a comeback. However, as its lifespan thus far has proven, it's harder to rely on high quality user-made games within a game than ever before in an age when people can just resort to using generative AI for an ever-increasing number of things.

#3731. GTA 6 players are already starting to get very good at heists, despite all the new challenges Rockstar has added to the game

Grand Theft Auto 6 has been out for a little while now, and already players are showing off their skills when it comes to the game's many heists. Despite the challenges in getting away clean, some are proving it's possible.

For one, sneaking into a bank while the vault is open and stuffing your bags full of marked bills is a tricky process of gradually making your way through rooms and taking out guards as quietly as possible. While the police in the clip below were called to an eventual breakout of violence, a lengthy getaway allowed for a cheeky payday of almost $100,000 in cash.

This crew really cracked a whole bank vault and walked out with almost $100K in GTA 6 💰🏦🚔😮‍💨 #gtavi #gta pic.twitter.com/pJyFXREBvY

One especially impressive element of Grand Theft Auto 6 is how many of its little mechanics interact with each other. As you can see below, if you bring a vehicle with a winch to a cash machine, you can actually pull it off the wall and drag it away from the scene of the crime.

Why rob a bank in GTA 6 when you can just take the whole ATM💸 How to do it❓- Hook the ATM up to a vehicle with a winch- Drag it through the streets until the cash cases fall out- Shoot them open and get out fast, the cops come quickly!(via u/MelloYello917) pic.twitter.com/5eXbULJWP3

As you progress through Grand Theft Auto 6, the game actually introduces you to both styles of heists. Without spoiling exactly how this happens, you're told how to go about taking on such criminal ventures, and you can continue to do so throughout the game at your pleasure. Still, even after you've been tutorialised, pulling off one of these heists is no joke, and can easily turn chaotic.

This GTA 6 robbery sequence was CRAZY, I couldn't even think straight . pic.twitter.com/l65xSFRoSr

Here's a little tip for those of you looking to pull off a heist yourself. You're told that safety deposit boxes can be rifled through for additional loot. However, when you actually make your way into a vault, these will be closed without much sign on which you can access. If you use the focus mode (by pushing in both L3 and R3), it will highlight boxes which you can shoot open. This, of course, may garner unwanted attention, so whether or not you think it's worth doing is part of the risk/reward dilemma you'll have to reckon with. As is the case with so much stuff in GTA 6 including, but not limited to, car-jacking.

If you're looking to get your life of crime properly underway, you can read our GTA 6 robberies page for a breakdown on how it works. Alternatively, for a wider view of the game, our GTA 6 walkthrough is the way to go.

In the latest chapter of the industry's collective embracing of AI, it was reported that Ubisoft was making the tech mandatory for upcoming projects, to the point teams had to justify why they didn't think it was suitable for their needs. The publisher has since put out a statement countering these claims.

"We encourage our teams to explore where AI can be useful and bring value to their work," Ubisoft tells Vertical Slice. "This doesn't mean that projects are required to use generative AI."

Earlier this week, Vertical Slice reported that Ubisoft now requires pitches for potential releases to demonstrate how they'd use gen-AI. Any team that objected to this apparently needed to state their case for why these tools weren't suitable for their requirements.

"Teams need to determine whether, and how, these technologies make sense for the game they want to make and the experience they want to create for players," Ubisoft's statement concludes.

According to the original report, anyone who didn't mention generative AI would automatically get a negative response to their proposal. This was all apparently mentioned in a meeting with senior staff.

It should be noted that gen-AI isn't said to be compulsory, but Ubisoft's investment is expected to be considerable. Regardless of the level of AI used within the bowels of the Assassin's Creed and Far Cry maker, it's but one of the many games companies embracing the tech.

EA, Activision, Capcom, and Square Enix are among those that have utilized AI to some degree in game creation. In some cases, generative assets were found and called out in released projects, including Call of Duty: Black Ops 7. Stats suggest that around 40% of game devs are using generative AI right now, but over half believe it's a net negative in the medium term.
